# Packages
```{r}
#| output: FALSE
library(tidyverse)
library(parallel)
library(tictoc)
library(knitr)
```

# Simulation - a1=0
```{r}
type1_f <- function(i) {
  set.seed(i + 2024)

  n <- 500     # sample size
  pz <- 0.2    # probability of Z = 1
  alpha0 <- 0  # logit probability of x = 1 in non-smokers (z = 0)    
  alpha1 <- 0  # log odds ratio of x = 1 in smokers (z = 1) vs non-smokers
  beta0 <- -3  # logit prob of y = 1 in non-coffee drinkers (x = 0) and non-smokers (z = 0)
  beta1 <- 0       
  beta2 <- 2

  # Generate a new dataset for this simulation
  z <- rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = pz)
  x <- rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = plogis(alpha0 + alpha1 * z))
  y <- rbinom(
    n, size = 1,
    prob = plogis(beta0 + beta1 * x + beta2 * z)
  )
  dat <- data.frame(lung = y, coffee = x, smoke = z)

  # Get the coffee p-value from each model
  p_unadjusted <- coef(summary(
    glm(lung ~ coffee, data = dat, family = binomial)
  ))["coffee", "Pr(>|z|)"]

  p_adjusted <- coef(summary(
    glm(lung ~ coffee + smoke, data = dat, family = binomial)
  ))["coffee", "Pr(>|z|)"]

  # Return whether each model rejects the null hypothesis
  c(unadjusted = p_unadjusted < 0.05,
    adjusted = p_adjusted < 0.05)
}

tictoc::tic()

cl <- parallel::makeCluster(5)
sim_out <- parallel::parLapply(cl, 1:1000, type1_f)
parallel::stopCluster(cl)

type1_rates_a0 <- colMeans(do.call(rbind, sim_out))
tictoc::toc()

type1_rates_a0

```

# Simulation - a1=2
```{r}
type1_f <- function(i) {
  set.seed(i + 2024)

  n <- 500     # sample size
  pz <- 0.2    # probability of Z = 1
  alpha0 <- 0  # logit probability of x = 1 in non-smokers (z = 0)    
  alpha1 <- 2  # log odds ratio of x = 1 in smokers (z = 1) vs non-smokers
  beta0 <- -3  # logit prob of y = 1 in non-coffee drinkers (x = 0) and non-smokers (z = 0)
  beta1 <- 0       
  beta2 <- 2

  # Generate a new dataset for this simulation
  z <- rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = pz)
  x <- rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = plogis(alpha0 + alpha1 * z))
  y <- rbinom(
    n, size = 1,
    prob = plogis(beta0 + beta1 * x + beta2 * z)
  )
  dat <- data.frame(lung = y, coffee = x, smoke = z)

  # Get the coffee p-value from each model
  p_unadjusted <- coef(summary(
    glm(lung ~ coffee, data = dat, family = binomial)
  ))["coffee", "Pr(>|z|)"]

  p_adjusted <- coef(summary(
    glm(lung ~ coffee + smoke, data = dat, family = binomial)
  ))["coffee", "Pr(>|z|)"]

  # Return whether each model rejects the null hypothesis
  c(unadjusted = p_unadjusted < 0.05,
    adjusted = p_adjusted < 0.05)
}

tictoc::tic()

cl <- parallel::makeCluster(5)
sim_out <- parallel::parLapply(cl, 1:1000, type1_f)
parallel::stopCluster(cl)

type1_rates_a2 <- colMeans(do.call(rbind, sim_out))
tictoc::toc()

type1_rates_a2

```

# Comparison of Results
```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
results_table <- data.frame(a1 = 0:2, Adjusted = c(
    unname(type1_rates_a0[2]),
    unname(type1_rates_a1[2]),
    unname(type1_rates_a2[2])), Unadjusted = c(unname(type1_rates_a0[1]), unname(type1_rates_a1[1]), unname(type1_rates_a2[1])))

kable(results_table, digits = 3)
```

When when a1=0, the adjusted and unadjusted models have the same p-value (0.043). Since this is below the significant level of 0.05, both models indicate a statistically significant association between drinking coffee and lung cancer. When a1 is 1 or 2, the p-values differ with the adjusted model's p-value remaining below 0.05 (statistically significant), while the unadjusted model's p-value is above 0.05 (not statistically significant). These findings suggest that when coffee consumption is associated with smoking, a potential confounder, the adjusted model should be used ot obtain a less biased estimate of the association between drinking coffee and lung cancer.
